title: Normalized restriction data for compact support on strict coefficient systems
statement: Fix $\ell\in\mathbf N$. A coefficient sequence is the finite commutative $\ell$-power-torsion sequence of [def-pur-etale-system-projection-data], and a map is a natural transformation of its inverse ring diagrams. For schemes and geometric maps use [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the actual varying-ring module categories on small pro-etale vertical sequence sites, their ordinary unbounded derived categories and the operations $j_!,p_*$, $J= D j_!$, $P=Rp_*$ of [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. Write $U_a$ for the restriction of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models] along the actual constant-sheaf coefficient map and $D U_a$ for its exact localization. Put $H_B=P_B\circ J_B$. A restriction-identification datum consists of ordinary composition $U_bU_a\cong U_{ab}$ and unit $U_{\mathrm{id}}\cong1$ maps that are identity on every section. Their derived maps are their exact localizations on the ordinary derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: the inverse localization-composition comparison followed by the localized ordinary identification. For $a:B_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ and $f:W\to V$, a geometric square consists of $f_{*,B}U_a^W\cong U_a^V f_{*,C}$ that is identity on every section, and $U_a^W f_C^*\cong f_B^*U_a^V$ whose inverse is its adjunction transpose [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. A normalized proper comparison is $P_BU_a^W\cong U_a^VP_C$ such that, for every K-injective $K$ over $C$ and every K-injective resolution $v:U_aK\to I$ over $B$, $p_{*,B}v$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the component is its inverse after the canonical derived-evaluation identifications. A normalized open comparison for open $j:X\hookrightarrow Z$ is $j_{!,B}U_a^X\cong U_a^Zj_{!,C}$ commuting with the original open-adjunction units and the specified inverse-image square. Define a compact-support comparison datum to comprise these geometric squares and these normalized open and proper comparisons; its derived compact-support isomorphism is the paste $P_B(a_j)$ followed by the proper comparison. These are specifications of data, not assumptions of existence.
